 AG, Hannah opposed Najib’s house arrest, declassified minutes show
 AG, Hannah opposed Najib’s house arrest, declassified minutes show
 18-Nov-2026, 12:54 18 Nov 2026, 12:54 FMT Reporters Share Two other FTPB members also voiced opposition to the house arrest, with one citing Najib Razak's other pending court cases.
 Former prime minister Najib Razak was placed under house arrest on Nov 10 under a conditional pardon after payment of his RM50 million fine in his SRC International case. 
 PETALING JAYA : Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar and federal territories minister Hannah Yeoh were against allowing Najib Razak to be placed under house arrest under a conditional pardon, according to the declassified minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) meeting. 
 According to the minutes, the AG held the view that the former prime minister should complete his reduced sentence in prison, until August 2028.
 Dusuki said there were no legal provisions for house arrest under the law, while the move would have implications on political stability, the country’s image at the international level, investments and the economy.
 “He stressed that the inmate should continue serving his sentence,” the minutes read, with Yeoh noted as sharing the same views.
 Former Federal Court judge Harmindar Singh Dhaliwal, another FTPB member, confirmed that there was no law on house arrest.
 However, he said Article 42 of the constitution makes reference to “pardons, reprieves and respites”, and argued that the Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim could exercise his discretion to grant a “respite”.
 Fellow FTPB member Razarudin Husain agreed with the views of the AG but said he would defer to the king’s final decision on the matter.
 Another board member, Supri Hashim, pointed out that Najib had several other cases pending before the courts, with further jail sentences possible.
 Dusuki also said Najib’s bankruptcy proceedings regarding more than RM1.7 billion in tax arrears should be taken into account by the board.
 However, the king said the tax arrears should be ignored as they had no relation to the pardon application and Najib had the right to defend his case in court.
 The minutes said the Agong then decided to grant the conditional pardon allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest upon payment of his RM50 million fine.
 Najib was jailed in August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction for abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving RM42 million in SRC International funds. He was sentenced to 12 years in jail and fined RM210 million.
 In January 2024, the then Agong, Al-Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah, halved Najib’s prison sentence and reduced his fine to RM50 million as part of a royal pardon.
 In September this year, the current Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, granted Najib a further conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
 This was subject to Najib paying the RM50 million fine and complying with other stipulated conditions.
 The former Pekan MP was placed under house arrest on Nov 10 after Umno helped pay the fine through crowdfunding.
